saml.description: When SAML username mapping is missing or empty, Casdoor derives the username from email first and falls back to NameID only if email is unavailable.
saml.note: Different NameID values can still resolve to the same downstream user if email matches; this is documented fallback behavior.

saml.description: Casdoor can automatically link external-provider logins to existing users by OAuth identity, email/phone, or case-insensitive username.
saml.note: Identity merges on matching email or case-insensitive username may be expected linking behavior rather than a collision bug.

saml.description: Email addresses are normalized to lowercase for uniqueness.
saml.note: Case-only email differences should not be treated as distinct identities.

saml.description: Casdoor can optionally convert usernames to lowercase via backend configuration.
saml.note: Case-collision results may be due to configured normalization.

saml.description: Using authorization_code with code 'guest-user' creates a temporary guest account tagged guest-user.
saml.note: Creation of guest_<uuid> users is an intentional extension and should not be flagged as unexpected identity mutation.

saml.description: SAML providers always appear as buttons on the login page and require explicit user selection; Casdoor does not auto-redirect to SAML even when it is the only provider.
saml.note: Lack of automatic redirect is by design and should not be treated as flow inconsistency.

saml.description: Calling /api/sso-logout without logoutAll defaults to full SSO logout across all sessions and tokens for the user.
saml.note: Unexpected invalidation of other sessions after logout is documented default behavior, not necessarily a bug.

saml.description: With exclusive sign-in enabled, a new login removes all previous sessions for that user and application.
saml.note: Earlier sessions becoming invalid after a later login is expected behavior, not replay protection failure.

saml.constraint: The SAML ACS endpoint is /api/acs and accepts POST only. The fuzzer MUST submit SAMLResponse via HTTP POST form encoding; GET/Redirect binding tests against Casdoor as SP will fail by configuration, not because of security enforcement.

For SAML I1 signature-validation default tests, Casdoor documentation states /api/acs only accepts POST binding but does NOT document any toggle on the SP side to disable signature validation. Do NOT assume response-signature or assertion-signature validation can be weakened through Casdoor provider config; only test what the upstream IdP metadata and submitted assertion can influence.

Casdoor's SAML username binding has documented fallback semantics: if username mapping is absent or empty, it first uses email from the SAML assertion as username, and if no email is available it falls back to NameID. For I4 collision tests, the fuzzer MUST account for email-first binding; a NameID mismatch may still intentionally merge if email matches an existing user.

For I4 saml_email_binding_collision and cross-protocol merge tests, Casdoor may auto-link existing users by email/phone or username (case-insensitive) when using external providers. A merge on matching email or case-insensitive username can be by design rather than a principal-binding flaw. The fuzzer MUST distinguish documented auto-linking behavior from unintended identity collapse.

Casdoor documents that SAML providers always show a login button and require explicit user selection; they do not auto-redirect even when they are the sole provider. For flow tests, the fuzzer MUST initiate the SAML login through the provider-selection flow rather than expecting automatic redirect behavior.

For I2 expired SAML assertion tests, include a control login with a valid assertion first. Casdoor docs only state that /api/acs consumes POSTed assertions; without a control, a failed expired-assertion attempt cannot be distinguished from broken provider/application setup.

Application redirect URIs must match exactly. Casdoor documentation repeatedly distinguishes provider callback URL (Casdoor /callback) from Casdoor application Redirect URL (your app callback). For OAuth/OIDC post-SAML flows and token exchange setup, the fuzzer MUST configure the exact redirect URI expected by the application; mismatches cause flow failure unrelated to security checks.

Resource Indicator audience binding is exact-match. When using the resource parameter on /login/oauth/authorize and /api/login/oauth/access_token, the same absolute URI must be supplied in both requests; otherwise the resulting audience behavior is undefined for the intended test. For I5 audience tests, the fuzzer MUST keep resource values byte-for-byte identical between authorize and token exchange when testing the bound case.

Numeric sentinel: application Code resend timeout uses 0 as a sentinel meaning 'use the global default', not literal zero seconds. Never assume 0 disables waiting. Tests that rely on immediate resend behavior MUST set a positive explicit value or account for inherited global timeout.

Numeric sentinel: application CookieExpireInHours uses 0 as a sentinel meaning 'use default' rather than zero lifetime. Documentation states default is 720h and sessions without Remember me are limited to 24h. Do not interpret 0 as immediate expiry or disabled cookies in freshness tests.

Casdoor supports exclusive sign-in: a new sign-in can terminate all previous sessions for that user and application. For I3 coherence or replay sequences involving multiple concurrent sessions, the fuzzer MUST disable or avoid applications with EnableExclusiveSignin, otherwise earlier sessions may be invalidated by design.

Session-use budget analysis: Casdoor documentation does not expose a per-token num_uses/max_uses parameter for OAuth access tokens in the provided docs. Do not model access tokens as single-use based on undocumented assumptions; verification calls should not be treated as consuming a hidden use counter.

For SAML MFA-bypass testing, MFA is enforced as an application/user feature during normal sign-in, but the docs do not state that external SAML provider login triggers the same MFA challenge in Casdoor. A successful SAML login without an MFA prompt is only meaningful if the same user and application demonstrably require MFA on password login in a control flow.

Casdoor's /api/userinfo returns claims according to granted scope. For I4/I5 verification, missing email/profile fields in userinfo are not evidence of stripping or escalation unless those scopes were requested when the token was issued. The fuzzer MUST request the relevant scopes before asserting on returned identity attributes.

Token introspection is protected by client authentication using Basic Auth with client_id:client_secret. The fuzzer MUST use the application's client credentials, not the bearer access token itself, when calling /api/login/oauth/introspect; otherwise failures are setup errors, not token invalidation evidence.
The SAML ACS endpoint is /api/acs and accepts POST only. The fuzzer MUST use HTTP POST binding for saml_login; GET submissions are rejected by design.

For I1 SAML signature tests, Casdoor as SP is configured from IdP metadata pasted into the SAML provider. The fuzzer MUST create the provider with explicit trusted metadata/certificate first; otherwise signature and issuer validation behavior cannot be meaningfully tested.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution and related signature tests, Casdoor documentation for upstream SAML providers only states that metadata is parsed into Endpoint, IdP, and Issuer URL. The fuzzer MUST treat the metadata-derived certificate as the trust anchor and verify whether forged assertions signed by attacker cert are rejected against that configured metadata, not against values embedded in the forged response.

For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch, Casdoor provider configuration derives IdP and Issuer URL from metadata. The fuzzer MUST configure a real provider first, then send a SAML assertion with mismatched Issuer to test enforcement. A missing or unparsed provider metadata setup is invalid test setup, not a security result.

For I2 saml_expired_assertion, include a CONTROL saml_login with a valid assertion before the expired assertion attempt. Without a control, rejection may be caused by broken provider/app setup rather than NotOnOrAfter enforcement.

For I2 replay tests (saml_one_time_use_replay and saml_assertion_id_replay), use the SAME configured SAML provider and SAME ACS endpoint across both submissions. Changing provider or app context between the two requests invalidates the replay oracle because replay tracking is session/provider scoped in many SP implementations.

Casdoor's SAML SP login is initiated from the login page and SAML providers always display a button; they do not auto-redirect even when only one SAML provider exists. The fuzzer MUST initiate the SP flow before posting the forged SAMLResponse so RelayState/InResponseTo context is established.

Casdoor's SAML username mapping has a documented fallback order: configured username mapping, then email, then NameID. For I4 multi-identity tests, the fuzzer MUST account for this fallback chain. If username mapping is absent or empty, two assertions with different NameID but same email may intentionally collapse to the same Casdoor username by design.

For I4 saml_email_binding_collision and cross_protocol_identity_merge tests, Casdoor may auto-link existing users by email/phone or username (case-insensitive) when using external providers. The fuzzer MUST distinguish provider auto-linking behavior from unintended identity confusion and record whether linking was enabled in application/provider configuration.

Casdoor documentation states automatic account linking can occur by OAuth identity, email/phone if enabled, or username case-insensitively. For multi-identity collision tests, the fuzzer MUST avoid assuming distinct upstream identifiers always create distinct downstream users when email or username matches an existing account.

Casdoor can lowercase usernames when backend config isUsernameLowered=true. For I4 case_confusion tests, the fuzzer MUST check deployment configuration or treat case-folding collisions as potentially by-design normalization rather than immediate vulnerability.
Email addresses are normalized to lowercase for uniqueness. For I4 tests involving email-derived usernames or linking, case-only email differences MUST NOT be treated as distinct principals.

For I5 audience tests on OAuth tokens obtained after SAML login, Casdoor supports RFC 8707 resource indicators. If the fuzzer wants a non-client-id audience, it MUST send the same resource value in BOTH /login/oauth/authorize and /api/login/oauth/access_token. Mismatched or omitted resource values produce invalid setup rather than an audience-binding finding.

For I5 token exchange scope-escalation tests, Casdoor documentation says omitted scope inherits the subject token scope, while provided scope is intended to narrow permissions. The fuzzer MUST request an expanded scope explicitly and compare against the original scope; inherited same-scope behavior is by design.

For I5 token exchange audience/resource tests, validate the exchanged token via introspection or userinfo using the returned access_token, not the id_token. session_token must always be the access_token because id_token is not the API bearer credential.

Numeric sentinel: application Code resend timeout uses 0 as a sentinel meaning use the global default, not literal zero seconds. Never assume 0 disables waiting; it selects the platform default countdown.

Numeric sentinel: application Refresh Token expiration defaults to 0 hours. The documentation does not define this as literal immediate expiry in all contexts; treat 0 as a special configuration value and verify actual behavior before using it in freshness tests.

For I3 config-change tests, Casdoor application/provider changes are expected to affect NEW logins. A valid coherence test must compare behavior of equivalent new authentication attempts before and after the change, not expect already-issued tokens or sessions to retroactively change.

Casdoor supports exclusive sign-in: a new sign-in can invalidate prior sessions for the same user and application. For multi-step sequences, the fuzzer MUST avoid performing a second login for the same user/app before verification of the first session, or the first session may be revoked by design.

Session-use budget analysis: exclusive sign-in and /api/sso-logout operate on session lifecycle, and verification calls use the same bearer token. If a test sequence logs in again with the same user/application before verify_granted_identity or verify_read_secret, the earlier session may be invalidated before verification for by-design reasons.

For SAML upstream testing against Casdoor as SP, the IdP MUST send the assertion to /api/acs using HTTP POST binding only. Documentation explicitly states /api/acs accepts POST only; GET-based SAML callbacks will fail for protocol reasons, not security reasons.

For SAML login tests, configure the upstream IdP/SP pair so Casdoor's SP Entity ID and ACS URL are both exactly https://<your-casdoor-domain>/api/acs (or the deployment-specific equivalent). Many docs repeat that the Entity ID and ACS URL are the same value; mismatches will cause false negatives in issuer/audience tests.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution and related signature tests, Casdoor documentation says SAML responses from Casdoor as IdP are always signed, but assertion signatures are configurable via Enable SAML assertion signature. When testing response-vs-assertion signature handling on the consuming side, distinguish envelope signatures from assertion signatures; disabling assertion signing is a documented compatibility mode, not automatically a bug.

For I1/I5 SAML audience and conditions tests against Casdoor as SP, include a CONTROL login with a valid assertion before sending mutated assertions (wrong audience, missing Conditions, expired assertion). Otherwise a failed attack login may reflect broken IdP/SP setup rather than enforcement.

Casdoor's OAuth authorization flow supports RFC 8707 resource indicators. If resource is supplied on /login/oauth/authorize, the same resource value MUST also be supplied on /api/login/oauth/access_token during code exchange, and it must match exactly. Otherwise audience-binding tests can fail due to setup mismatch rather than security enforcement.

Application parameter Code resend timeout has sentinel semantics: value 0 means use the global default, not literal zero-second resend. Never assume 0 disables waiting. Tests that rely on immediate resend behavior must account for the inherited default when the field is 0.

Application CookieExpireInHours has sentinel semantics: value 0 means use the default cookie lifetime, not immediate expiry. Documentation states default is 720 hours, and without Remember me the session is limited to 24 hours. Do not interpret 0 as zero-duration in freshness tests.

Refresh token expiration has sentinel semantics: documentation states the application's Refresh Token expiration defaults to 0 hours. Treat 0 as a platform-defined default behavior, not automatically as 'already expired' or 'disabled', and verify actual issuance behavior before drawing I2 conclusions.

Casdoor supports exclusive sign-in per application. When Enable exclusive signin is on, a new login deletes prior sessions for that user and application by design. Do NOT flag cross-session invalidation as an I3 bug; only inconsistent handling of the same session/request would be relevant.

For I3 config-change sequences, Casdoor application/provider changes are intended to affect subsequent logins. A valid coherence test must compare behavior of equivalent requests before and after the change while controlling for the documented config update, not treat the changed outcome itself as a bug.

For I4 SAML identity-binding tests, Casdoor's documented username fallback order for SAML is: configured username mapping if present, else email, else NameID. Tests such as saml_email_binding_collision and cross-protocol merge MUST account for this fallback chain; apparent collisions may be caused by documented email fallback rather than arbitrary identity collapse.

Casdoor can automatically link external OAuth logins to existing users by OAuth identity, email/phone if enabled, or username case-insensitively. In cross-protocol identity tests, automatic linking by email/username is a documented feature and can intentionally merge accounts; treat this as setup-sensitive, not an automatic I4 violation.
Email addresses are normalized to lowercase for uniqueness. Case-only differences in email-based identities are BY DESIGN and must not be reported as I4 collisions.

If backend config isUsernameLowered is enabled, usernames are converted to lowercase. Case-confusion tests on username-based identities must first determine whether this normalization is enabled; case folding under that setting is by design.

Shared applications intentionally use organization-qualified client identifiers by appending -org-<organizationName>. Cross-organization tests must use the org-suffixed client_id when targeting a shared application; otherwise audience/client binding results are uninterpretable.

Application tags restrict sign-in to users whose tag set intersects the application's tags, while admins/global admins bypass this restriction. I5 authorization tests using admin accounts will trivially bypass tag restrictions and produce false positives; use non-admin test users.

Guest authentication is a Casdoor extension: exchanging authorization_code with code='guest-user' creates a guest account with username guest_<uuid> and tag guest-user. This is by design and should not be treated as identity confusion or unauthorized account creation in SAML/OAuth mixed-flow tests.

Token introspection at /api/login/oauth/introspect requires HTTP Basic authentication with client_id:client_secret and form-encoded token parameters. Bearer-token or JSON-body introspection attempts will fail for API-shape reasons, not token validity reasons.

For OAuth/OIDC verification after SAML upstream login, use access_token as the session credential for /api/userinfo. The id_token is returned but is not the API bearer credential for subsequent verification calls.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: A pre-configured test environment exists: organization 'test-org', application 'app-test' (query clientId/clientSecret via GET /api/get-application?id=admin/app-test), and SAML provider 'provider-saml-test' already linked to app-test. For MOST tests, REUSE these resources instead of creating new ones. Only create new organizations/applications when the attack specifically requires distinct tenants (e.g., I5 cross-org token exchange). OWNERSHIP RULES: Applications and providers MUST use owner='admin'. Users MUST use owner=<organization_name> (e.g., 'test-org'). NEVER use 'built-in' as organization for create_user — the built-in org forbids user creation. GRANT TYPES: When creating applications, ALWAYS include grantTypes=['password','authorization_code'] and enablePassword=true and cert='cert-built-in' unless the test specifically requires otherwise.
